question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode to agent-core, and should it extend the existing toolExecution contract or wait for tool concurrency-safety metadata first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested change alters core runtime ordering, security/approval timing, transcript semantics, and likely adds a new opt-in execution surface.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this open and require an owner design for execute-on-parse with ordering, hook, approval, cancellation, transcript, and concurrency-safety tests.

options.title: Defer Until Tool Metadata
options.body: Treat this as blocked on a broader concurrency-safety/tool-classification contract such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 before changing scheduling.

options.title: Keep Post-Stream Semantics
options.body: Reject or close the direction if maintainers want current post-stream parallel batching to remain the only supported tool-execution model.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this open and require an owner design for execute-on-parse with ordering, hook, approval, cancellation, transcript, and concurrency-safety tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across agent-core extraction, provider stream handling, and tool-call correctness changes implicated by the design choice.
